chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from someone else from Al-Sha'iri from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever spends the night awake regarding his earnings and does not give his eyes their share of sleep, then that earning is prohibited.
ai.seo_question: What makes earnings haram due to neglecting sleep?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights that neglecting the 'eye's due' (sleep) for the sake of excessive work renders earnings haram, emphasizing that health preservation is a prerequisite for lawful sustenance. Scholars interpret 'sahar' (staying awake late) here not merely as night vigilance for worship, but as compulsive overwork that disrupts the body's natural rhythm, thereby invalidating the blessing (barakah) in one's wealth. This principle underscores the Islamic view that the means of earning must not compromise the physical well-being mandated by God.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, form Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from someone else, from Al Shairy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who spends the night in wakefulness regarding the earnings and does not give the eyes its share from the sleep, so his earning that is Prohibited’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from more than one person from al-Shu’ayriy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one works the whole night without giving the eyes their share of sleep, such earning is unlawful.’”
